title: Fabled Realm
description: A Pokémon-inspired creature-catching game built for A-Level Computer Science coursework. Pick a starter, catch monsters out in the world, and battle with your team. The battle system was refactored from tangled procedural code into a state machine partway through development for maintainability.
roadmap_note: Made before I had come up with the idea to add online web-demo, sorry!!

title: This Portfolio Website (Original)
tagline: The first version of this site — kept as a before-and-after
description: The original version of my portfolio: a single scrolling page where each project section fetched its README straight from GitHub at load time and rendered it with Marked.js, so editing a README updated the live site with no rebuild. A clever trick, but it forced every kind of content — including things that weren't code projects at all — into a markdown-shaped box. Kept live and unmodified as a deliberate before-and-after against this rebuild.

title: Predictive Pokémon Outcome Modelling
description: A machine learning project exploring what predicts the outcome of a one-on-one Pokémon battle. Built a logistic regression classifier over ~27,000 simulated Generation 1 matchups, using base stats and feature engineering (Cartesian products of stat pairs) to predict a winner, then evaluated it with a confusion matrix.
roadmap_note: Made before I had come up with the idea to add online web-demo, sorry!!

title: Bingo Board
tagline: Custom bingo boards for game nights with friends
description: A digital bingo board for tracking the funny, frustrating, and recurring events that happen during group gaming sessions. Board options are editable in a text file, squares are randomised on each launch, and clicking a square marks it with a gold cross.
roadmap_note: Made before I had come up with the idea to add online web-demo, sorry!!

title: This Portfolio Website (Rebuild)
tagline: The site you're viewing right now
description: A full rebuild of my personal site as a new repo, kept separate from the original so the growth between them stays visible. Content is data-driven (JSON files feeding experience/education/project pages) rather than hardcoded markup, and I built a self-service admin tool so I can add new entries without touching HTML or CSS. The hub itself is a Friv/CoolMathGames-style project player.
